title.narrative: Strengthening Farmers' Linkage to the Avocado Value Chain in Yoro, Honduras

description.narrative: Original blurb on website: Small-scale avocado farmers in the Yoro department of Honduras currently struggle to get their avocados to market, which leaves them vulnerable to exploitative prices. The IAF supports community-led solutions to expand economic opportunities that provide productive alternatives to irregular migration. Our grantee Fundacin para la Investigacin Participativa con Agricultores de Honduras (FIPAH) helps small-scale farmers earn more from avocado sales by increasing sustainable production and by strengthening the Yoro Association of Local Agricultural Research Committees? ability to (ASOCIAL) to collect and market avocados. FIPAH?s activities also promote women and youth?s participation in producing and selling avocados and provide opportunities for farmers to share their knowledge about production techniques in national forums. This grant is part of the IAF?s efforts to address the root causes of irregular migration in Central America. FY24 Amendment blurb: This amendment provides FIPAH with an additional two years and $263,000 to continue to build the capacity of organized groups of avocado farmers in Yoro department of Honduras to increase the volume of high-quality avocados for sale and articulate local and departmental production with the value chain for this crop of growing importance. ASOCIAL will aim to increase volume sold year over year and cover basic operating costs of its collection facility. FIPAH?s efforts in sustainable agriculture and economic development will diversify sources of household incomes. As part of the amendment, FIPAH is mobilizing an additional $238,150 in counterpart funding to the grant agreement.
